name: Professional Services
title: Engagement delivery evidence coordinator
summary: Connect client requirements, delivery evidence, staffing constraints, and commercial scope before engagement leaders commit changes.
situation: Illustrative architecture: A consulting team prepares a milestone review for a client transformation program. Deliverables are spread across workspaces, acceptance criteria live in a statement of work, and staffing changes affect the schedule. Agents assemble a review packet while engagement leaders retain client commitments and professional judgments.
problem: A polished progress summary can treat an uploaded draft as an accepted deliverable or omit a scope change hidden in meeting notes. Reusing prior-client examples also risks confidentiality leakage when shared knowledge stores lack engagement boundaries.
whyAgents: Scope, delivery-evidence, capacity, and briefing specialists inspect distinct systems. A milestone workflow separates contractual criteria, observed evidence, and proposed changes so leaders can make a concrete decision.
outcome: The intended result is a reviewable operational decision with source evidence and explicit ownership. Measure preparation effort and unrecognized delivery gaps, not just report throughput. A useful assistant makes commitments and evidence easier to inspect while preserving professional accountability and client confidentiality.

agents.name: Scope evidence agent
agents.responsibility: Retrieve signed scope and approved changes with acceptance criteria.
agents.boundary: Cannot interpret disputed terms as a binding legal conclusion or expand scope.

agents.name: Delivery verifier
agents.responsibility: Match deliverable versions to required review and acceptance evidence.
agents.boundary: Cannot mark client acceptance from internal draft status.

agents.name: Capacity planner
agents.responsibility: Compare approved work with staffing availability and dependencies.
agents.boundary: Cannot assign staff or promise dates without leader approval.

agents.name: Client briefing agent
agents.responsibility: Draft status, unresolved decisions, and proposed next steps with citations.
agents.boundary: Cannot contact clients or issue commercial commitments autonomously.

systems.name: Engagement management platform
systems.role: Owns milestones, assignments, approved plans, and commercial change records.

systems.name: Client document workspace
systems.role: Stores scoped artifacts and explicit internal or client acceptance states.

systems.name: Resource and finance systems
systems.role: Supply staffing availability, budget facts, and approved billing data through role-limited adapters.

flow.title: Open milestone review
flow.description: Bind the review to engagement, reporting date, contract revision, and accountable delivery leader.

flow.title: Collect acceptance criteria
flow.description: Retrieve signed scope and approved changes; retain unresolved commercial questions separately from operational requirements.

flow.title: Inspect delivery evidence
flow.description: Map each criterion to the exact artifact version and acceptance record, exposing missing or provisional evidence.

flow.title: Evaluate capacity constraints
flow.description: Run bounded schedule scenarios using actual availability and dependencies without assuming overtime or unapproved role substitutions.

flow.title: Prepare leader decision
flow.description: Show accepted work, remaining gaps, forecast assumptions, and proposed client questions for engagement-leader review.

flow.title: Record approved commitments
flow.description: Publish the reviewed report or change request through existing channels and track client acknowledgement independently of internal approval.

failures.scenario: An internal draft is mistaken for client acceptance.
failures.detection: Acceptance registry lacks the required client signoff for the artifact version.
failures.recovery: Mark the milestone unaccepted and request the missing review without rewriting the historical status.

failures.scenario: A retrieved example belongs to a restricted prior engagement.
failures.detection: Engagement access policy rejects the document's client and purpose attributes.
failures.recovery: Exclude it and use an approved reusable asset or independently authored example.

controls: Enforce client and engagement isolation across retrieval, caches, and report exports.
Distinguish draft, internally reviewed, client-submitted, and client-accepted deliverables.
Bind commercial commitments to signed scope and approved change records.
Require leader approval before client communications, staffing assignments, or schedule promises.
Exclude confidential personnel and billing details from broad delivery summaries.

metrics.name: Acceptance evidence coverage
metrics.definition: Milestone criteria linked to valid acceptance evidence divided by criteria claimed complete.

metrics.name: Review preparation time
metrics.definition: Time from reporting cutoff to leader-reviewable milestone packet.

metrics.name: Forecast revision rate
metrics.definition: Published forecasts changed after unrecorded capacity or scope facts emerge divided by published forecasts.

metrics.name: Confidentiality filter quality
metrics.definition: Authorized reusable assets correctly available and restricted client assets correctly denied in a curated evaluation.

tradeoffs.benefit: Prevents activity volume from masquerading as delivered value.
tradeoffs.cost: Requires explicit acceptance metadata from client workflows.
Resource data may lag informal assignments or absences.
Reduces convenient reuse unless knowledge is deliberately approved for sharing.

rollout.acceptance: Leaders verify acceptance states, scope changes, and restricted-client retrieval using known cases.
One delivery team reviews draft packets and checks forecast assumptions without client publication.
Reviewed reports launch after stale-acceptance, access-boundary, and scope-revision exercises pass.
